chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the slave: A man gives money to him to buy himself and then free him. He said, 'It is not valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a slave buying his own freedom with money given by his master?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the specific mechanism of a master giving a slave funds to purchase their own freedom is deemed legally insufficient ('la yaslahu'), distinguishing it from the formal contract of *kitabah*. This ruling highlights the strict procedural requirements in Shia jurisprudence for manumission, emphasizing that mere provision of funds does not automatically establish the binding legal status of self-purchase without proper contractual formalities. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the nuances of slave emancipation and the rights of the *mukatab* within the broader framework of Islamic civil law.
